subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: Boundary refinement of claim.law.offsetof-rename-can-regress-prior-improved-fn: when that law's hazard fires (a hand-tuned prior-IMPROVED function regressing from a constant respell on one pressure-critical base), switching the respell to the OTHER known typed form does not evade it. Verified on the law's own origin function, critter.c CritterInitGeo (real 63, atan2-operand-staged): the parent law recorded offsetof-on-raw regressions on base c (63->113 and 63->86); this session's retry through the function's own pre-existing file-local view struct (typed member access, no offsetof, no cast-on-load -- the form that elsewhere DIVERGES from offsetof per claim.law.typed-global-member-vs-view-cast-diverges) regressed with the SAME signature and, for the movePath block, the SAME magnitude (yaw pair: 63->106; movePath block: 63->86). Signature both times: ours-only addi chain at function ENTRY (insn 3-4) replacing the target's single mr -- i.e. MWCC stops copying the incoming base with mr and instead materializes a dedicated derived-address register as soon as the count of typed accesses on that base crosses the level the hand-tuned state was balanced at (the function already carries two byte-stable view-member uses; adding more tips it). CONSEQUENCE: a per-base veto from the parent law covers ALL typed spellings, not just offsetof -- do not spend probes cycling offsetof/view/member forms on a vetoed base; the raw int-literal addend is load-bearing there. The remaining escape routes are a WebFrank REGISTER_ONLY rule for the entry seam or revisiting after the function's own residual is closed. Distinct from claim.law.typed-global-member-vs-view-cast-diverges: that law says the two forms differ from EACH OTHER in general; this one says that under the parent law's hazard both land on the same wrong side.
